hints.text: Compare prior times likelihood for the two dice.
The unnormalized weights are (1/2)(1/6) for A and (1/2)(1/2) for B.

solution.setup: Apply Bayes' rule with equal prior probabilities.
solution.reasoning: The probability weight for A is 1/12 and for B is 1/4. Normalize: (1/4)/(1/12+1/4)=(3/12)/(4/12).
solution.sanityCheck: A six is three times as likely under B, so equal priors produce posterior odds 3:1.

keyInsight: Posterior odds equal prior odds multiplied by the likelihood ratio.
recognitionCues: An observed outcome changes the probability of a hidden source.
commonMistakes: Answering 1/2 because the die was chosen uniformly before observing the roll.
followUps: What is the posterior after two consecutive sixes?

source.notes: Original variant of a publicly reported interview family associated with IMC, Optiver.

title: Which Die Produced the Six?
problem: Choose one of two dice uniformly. Die A is fair. Die B rolls a 6 with probability 1/2 and each other face with probability 1/10. The chosen die is rolled once and shows 6. What is the probability Die B was chosen?
